data.name: Chughtai
data.gender_notes: Chughtai is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A person skilled in arts, painting, or calligraphy. The name Chughtai carries the meaning “Artist” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Persian, Urdu. Parents who choose Chughtai usually hope their child will grow to embody artist and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Chughtai belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Artist.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Chughtai total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Chughtai holds significant cultural importance in the Islamic world, particularly in the region of the Indian subcontinent. It is a name associated with excellence and artistic creativity. Alive in the medieval Islamic civilization, Hussain Bicchu, also known as Chughtai, was an accomplished painter, known for his miniature paintings in Indian subcontinent. His works have been an inspiration for generations of artists and art enthusiasts. The name Chughtai also evokes a sense of pride and respect for the rich artistic heritage of the Islamic world and the Indian subcontinent.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Chughtai also carries spiritual significance in the Islamic tradition. The Arabic term 'Sunnah' means both convenant or tradition and a specific behavior of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). In this context, the name Chughtai can be seen as an embodiment of the Sunnah in the field of art, craftsmanship, and creativity. As a person skillful in arts, a Chughtai strives to constantly improve and innovate their craft while adhering to the principles and values espoused in the traditions of their cultural and spiritual heritage. In essence, the name encapsulates the spirit of creating beauty in the world as an expression of divine inspiration and purpose.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Chughtai is believed to originate from the Persian word 'Chah-gard', meaning 'four corners of the earth'. This suggests a deep connection to the vastness and interconnectedness of the universe. It can also be seen as a reminder of the Prophet Muhammad's (pbuh) mission to spread the message of Islam to all corners of the world.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: Khwaja Abdul Rahman Chughtai (1897–1975) was a Pakistani painter and calligrapher, who is considered one of the greatest artists of the 20th century in Pakistan. He was born in the village of Chughtai in the Peshawar District of the North-West Frontier Province, British India.

Mīr Sayyid Alam Chughtai (1315–1389) was a leading Persian painter, calligrapher and poet from Herat, in present-day Afghanistan, during the Timurid Empire. He was a student of the renowned painter Amir 'Ali Sarwani. Chughtai was a master of the Lahore style of painting, which was characterized by its delicate and precise execution.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Chughtai is widely recognized in the context of Islamic art, South Asian art, and contemporary art. Chughtai's works have been highly sought-after in art auctions at prestigious houses such as Christie's and Sotheby's. His art is also regularly exhibited in galleries and museums around the world. Chughtai's unique style, which blended traditional Islamic and Persian art with modern influences, continues to inspire artists and collectors alike.
